title: 1931 Avro Ten Southern Cloud disappearance
summary: An airline aircraft carrying eight people crashed in the Snowy Mountains during a scheduled flight from Sydney to Melbourne. The aircraft was 25 kilometers off course, and investigation concluded severe weather conditions much worse than forecast most likely contributed to the crash. The wreckage was not discovered for 27 years, found in heavily timbered mountainous terrain facing the wrong direction.
probable_cause: Severe weather conditions at the time of the flight most likely contributed to the crash

factors.evidence: Weather conditions en route were hazardous and much worse than predicted
crash site was in heavily timbered mountainous terrain about 25 km east of the direct Sydney–Melbourne route and wreckage was facing the wrong direction
aircraft crashed in the Snowy Mountains

events.text: Southern Cloud departed Sydney for Melbourne at 8:10 AM
Aircraft encountered hazardous weather much worse than predicted
Aircraft crashed in Snowy Mountains terrain 25 km east of direct route

notes: Aircraft disappeared in 1931 but wreckage not discovered until 1958; investigation findings based on wreckage analysis and weather records

title: TWA 599
summary: A Fokker F-10 crashed shortly after takeoff from Kansas City on the first leg to Wichita, killing all eight aboard including Notre Dame football coach Knute Rockne. Moisture had entered the interior of one wooden wing over time, weakening the glue bonds connecting the wing structure. One spar failed, the wing developed uncontrolled flutter and separated from the aircraft. The crash brought about significant changes in airplane safety and forced the industry to adopt all-metal aircraft designs.
probable_cause: Structural failure of the wooden wing caused by moisture penetration that weakened the glue bonding the wing laminate.

factors.evidence: The wings of Fokker Trimotors were made of wood laminate vulnerable to moisture
moisture had entered the interior of one wing over a period but was not detected in-service
wooden aircraft design proved structurally vulnerable and forced the industry to adopt all-metal aircraft and advance design standards
One spar finally failed; the wing developed uncontrolled flutter and separated from the aircraft

events.text: The Transcontinental and Western Air scheduled flight was from Kansas City to Los Angeles with a stopover in Wichita on March 31, 1931.
The co-pilot's radio call to Wichita indicated the weather here is getting tough and the crew planned to turn around and go back to Kansas City.
The wooden wing became moist over time, causing the glue connecting the wing to the fuselage to weaken, allowing one spar to fail.
One spar finally failed and the wing developed uncontrolled flutter and separated from the aircraft near Bazaar, Kansas, killing all eight occupants.

title: 1931 Jinan air crash
summary: A Stinson Detroiter carrying two experienced pilots and a passenger departed Nanjing bound for Beiping on November 19, 1931. After refueling at Xu Zhou, the aircraft encountered severe fog while navigating over Jinan by visual landmarks. The crew lost sight of the railway they were following and, unable to locate their destination airport, descended progressively below safe altitudes seeking visual reference. The aircraft struck West Mountain and broke apart, killing all three aboard.
probable_cause: The crew descended below minimum safe altitude while attempting to visually locate their destination airport in conditions of low visibility and inadequate communication between pilots. The presence of two pilots in a single-pilot designed cockpit, with the captain seated as a passenger while the first officer was at the controls, contributed to insufficient cross-check and warning.

factors.evidence: aircraft encountered severe fog and began flying off course
pilot lost the railway in his sight, kept on heading for the nearby Wujiapu Airport
pilot could not know his exact altitude, disoriented and failed to realize plane was descending slowly
pilot descended the aircraft beneath the minimum safety altitude while attempting to seek their target, Wujiapu airport
lack of communication between the pilots also played a major role, captain sitting in passenger seat should have reminded pilot that flight was dangerously close to terrain
aircraft hit the peak of West Mountain and broke off its right wing, crashed into the valley below

events.text: The Stinson Detroiter took off around 8:00 am local time
The plane landed at Xu Zhou Airport for refueling near 10:00 am, and took off again 10 minutes later with captain moving to the passenger seat while first officer Liang took controls
It then flew into Jinan airspace and the aircraft encountered severe fog and began flying off course
The pilot lost the railway in his sight, so he kept on heading for the nearby Wujiapu Airport
The plane started to descend while the pilot headed to the northwest for the target airport
After the plane passed the waypoint in Changqing District, the aircraft hit the peak of what is now called West Mountain below the summit and broke off its right wing
This put the plane into a rapidly descending spiral and the Detroiter crashed into the valley below and disintegrated

notes: text is comprehensive with detailed investigation findings
passenger was notable poet Xu Zhimo, adding to historical significance
